   247→    Commit: hash,
   248→    Mode:   git.HardReset,

   250→
   251→// CORRECT - use git CLI

   262→
   263→Git commands like `git status` and `worktree.Status()` return paths relative to the **repository root**, not the current working directory. When an agent runs from a subdirectory (e.g., `/repo/frontend`), using `os.Getwd()` to construct absolute paths will produce incorrect results for files in sibling directories.

   265→```go
   266→// WRONG - breaks when running from subdirectory
   267→cwd, _ := os.Getwd()  // e.g., /repo/frontend
   268→absPath := filepath.Join(cwd, file)  // file="api/src/types.ts" → /repo/frontend/api/src/types.ts (WRONG)
   269→
   270→// CORRECT - use repo root
   271→repoRoot, _ := paths.WorktreeRoot()
   272→absPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, file)  // → /repo/api/src/types.ts (CORRECT)
   273→```
   274→
   275→This also affects path filtering. The `paths.ToRelativePath()` function rejects paths starting with `..`, so computing relative paths from cwd instead of repo root will filter out files in sibling directories:

   278→// WRONG - filters out sibling directory files
   279→cwd, _ := os.Getwd()  // /repo/frontend
   280→relPath := paths.ToRelativePath("/repo/api/file.ts", cwd)  // returns "" (filtered out as "../api/file.ts")
   281→
   282→// CORRECT - keeps all repo files
   283→repoRoot, _ := paths.WorktreeRoot()
   284→relPath := paths.ToRelativePath("/repo/api/file.ts", repoRoot)  // returns "api/file.ts"
   285→```
   286→
   287→**When to use `os.Getwd()`:** Only when you actually need the current directory (e.g., finding agent session directories that are cwd-relative).
   288→
   289→**When to use repo root:** Any time you're working with paths from git status, git diff, or any git-relative file list.

   317→- Rewind restores files from shadow branch commit tree (does not use `git reset`)

   319→- Tracks session state in `.git/entire-sessions/` (shared across worktrees)
   320→- **Shadow branch migration** - if user does stash/pull/rebase (HEAD changes without commit), shadow branch is automatically moved to new base commit

   357→#### Session Phase State Machine
   358→
   359→Sessions track their lifecycle through phases managed by a state machine in `session/phase.go`:
   360→
   361→**Phases:** `ACTIVE`, `IDLE`, `ENDED`
   362→
   363→**Events:**
   364→
   365→- `TurnStart` - Agent begins a turn (UserPromptSubmit hook)
   366→- `TurnEnd` - Agent finishes a turn (Stop hook)
   367→- `GitCommit` - A git commit was made (PostCommit hook)
   368→- `SessionStart` - New session started
   369→- `SessionStop` - Session explicitly stopped
   370→

   372→
   373→- `IDLE + TurnStart → ACTIVE` - Agent starts working
   374→- `ACTIVE + TurnEnd → IDLE` - Agent finishes turn
   375→- `ACTIVE + GitCommit → ACTIVE` - User commits while agent is working (condense immediately)
   376→- `IDLE + GitCommit → IDLE` - User commits between turns (condense immediately)
   377→- `ENDED + GitCommit → ENDED` - Post-session commit (condense if files touched)
   378→
   379→The state machine emits **actions** (e.g., `ActionCondense`, `ActionUpdateLastInteraction`) that hook handlers dispatch to strategy-specific implementations.
   380→
   381→#### Metadata Structure
   382→
   383→**Shadow Strategy** - Shadow branches (`entire/<commit-hash[:7]>-<worktreeHash[:6]>`):
   384→
   385→```
   386→.entire/metadata/<session-id>/
   387→├── full.jsonl               # Session transcript
   388→├── prompt.txt               # User prompts
   389→├── context.md               # Generated context
   390→└── tasks/<tool-use-id>/     # Task checkpoints
   391→    ├── checkpoint.json      # UUID mapping for rewind
   392→    └── agent-<id>.jsonl     # Subagent transcript
   393→```
   394→
   395→**Both Strategies** - Metadata branch (`entire/checkpoints/v1`) - sharded checkpoint format:
   396→
   397→```
   398→<checkpoint-id[:2]>/<checkpoint-id[2:]>/
   399→├── metadata.json            # CheckpointSummary (aggregated stats)
   400→├── 0/                       # First session (0-based indexing)
   401→│   ├── metadata.json        # Session-specific metadata
   402→│   ├── full.jsonl           # Session transcript
   403→│   ├── prompt.txt           # User prompts
   404→│   ├── context.md           # Generated context
   405→│   ├── content_hash.txt     # SHA256 of transcript
   406→│   └── tasks/<tool-use-id>/ # Task checkpoints (if applicable)
   407→│       ├── checkpoint.json  # UUID mapping
   408→│       └── agent-<id>.jsonl # Subagent transcript
   409→├── 1/                       # Second session (if multiple sessions)
   410→│   ├── metadata.json
   411→│   ├── full.jsonl
   412→│   └── ...
   413→└── ...
   414→```
   415→
   416→**Multi-session metadata.json format:**
   417→
   418→```json
   419→{
   420→  "checkpoint_id": "abc123def456",
   421→  "session_id": "2026-01-13-uuid", // Current/latest session
   422→  "session_ids": ["2026-01-13-uuid1", "2026-01-13-uuid2"], // All sessions
   423→  "session_count": 2, // Number of sessions in this checkpoint
   424→  "strategy": "manual-commit",
   425→  "created_at": "2026-01-13T12:00:00Z",
   426→  "files_touched": ["file1.txt", "file2.txt"] // Merged from all sessions
   427→}
   428→```
   429→
   430→When multiple sessions are condensed to the same checkpoint (same base commit):
   431→
   432→- Sessions are stored in numbered subfolders using 0-based indexing (`0/`, `1/`, `2/`, etc.)
   433→- Latest session is always in the highest-numbered folder
   434→- `session_ids` array tracks all sessions, `session_count` increments
   435→
   436→**Session State** (filesystem, `.git/entire-sessions/`):
   437→
   438→```
   439→<session-id>.json            # Active session state (base_commit, checkpoint_count, etc.)
   440→```
   441→
   442→#### Checkpoint ID Linking
   443→
   444→Both strategies use a **12-hex-char random checkpoint ID** (e.g., `a3b2c4d5e6f7`) as the stable identifier linking user commits to metadata.
   445→
   446→**How checkpoint IDs work:**
   447→
   448→1. **Generated once per checkpoint**: When condensing session metadata to the metadata branch
   449→
   450→2. **Added to user commits** via `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer:
   451→   - **Manual-commit**: Added via `prepare-commit-msg` hook (user can remove it before committing)
   452→
   453→3. **Used for directory sharding** on `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch:
   454→   - Path format: `<id[:2]>/<id[2:]>/`
   455→   - Example: `a3b2c4d5e6f7` → `a3/b2c4d5e6f7/`
   456→   - Creates 256 shards to avoid directory bloat
   457→
   458→4. **Appears in commit subject** on `entire/checkpoints/v1` commits:
   459→   - Format: `Checkpoint: a3b2c4d5e6f7`
   460→   - Makes `git log entire/checkpoints/v1` readable and searchable
   461→
   462→**Bidirectional linking:**
   463→
   464→```
   465→User commit → Metadata:
   466→  Extract "Entire-Checkpoint: a3b2c4d5e6f7" trailer
   467→  → Read a3/b2c4d5e6f7/ directory from entire/checkpoints/v1 tree at HEAD
   468→
   469→Metadata → User commits:
   470→  Given checkpoint ID a3b2c4d5e6f7
   471→  → Search user branch history for commits with "Entire-Checkpoint: a3b2c4d5e6f7" trailer
   472→```
   473→
   474→Note: Commit subjects on `entire/checkpoints/v1` (e.g., `Checkpoint: a3b2c4d5e6f7`) are
   475→for human readability in `git log` only. The CLI always reads from the tree at HEAD.
   476→
   477→**Example:**
   478→
   479→```
   480→User's commit (on main branch):
   481→  "Implement login feature
   482→
   483→  Entire-Checkpoint: a3b2c4d5e6f7"
   484→       ↓ ↑
   485→       Linked via checkpoint ID
   486→       ↓ ↑
   487→entire/checkpoints/v1 commit:
   488→  Subject: "Checkpoint: a3b2c4d5e6f7"
   489→
   490→  Tree: a3/b2c4d5e6f7/
   491→    ├── metadata.json (checkpoint_id: "a3b2c4d5e6f7")
   492→    ├── full.jsonl (session transcript)
   493→    ├── prompt.txt
   494→    └── context.md
   495→```
   496→
   497→#### Commit Trailers
   498→
   499→**On user's active branch commits (both strategies):**
   500→
   501→- `Entire-Checkpoint: <checkpoint-id>` - 12-hex-char ID linking to metadata on `entire/checkpoints/v1`
   502→  - Auto-commit: Always added when creating commits
   503→  - Manual-commit: Added by hook; user can remove to skip linking
   504→
   505→**On shadow branch commits (`entire/<commit-hash[:7]>-<worktreeHash[:6]>`) - manual-commit only:**
   506→
   507→- `Entire-Session: <session-id>` - Session identifier
   508→- `Entire-Metadata: <path>` - Path to metadata directory within the tree
   509→- `Entire-Task-Metadata: <path>` - Path to task metadata directory (for task checkpoints)
   510→- `Entire-Strategy: manual-commit` - Strategy that created the commit
   511→
   512→**On metadata branch commits (`entire/checkpoints/v1`) - both strategies:**
   513→
   514→Commit subject: `Checkpoint: <checkpoint-id>` (or custom subject for task checkpoints)
   515→
   516→Trailers:
   517→
   518→- `Entire-Session: <session-id>` - Session identifier
   519→- `Entire-Strategy: <strategy>` - Strategy name (manual-commit)
   520→- `Entire-Agent: <agent-name>` - Agent name (optional, e.g., "Claude Code")
   521→- `Ephemeral-branch: <branch>` - Shadow branch name (optional)
   522→- `Entire-Metadata-Task: <path>` - Task metadata path (optional, for task checkpoints)
   523→
   524→**Note:** Manual-commit keeps active branch history clean - the only addition to user commits is the single `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer. Manual-commit never creates commits on the active branch (user creates them manually). All detailed session data (transcripts, prompts, context) is stored on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` orphan branch or shadow branches.
   525→
   526→#### Multi-Session Behavior
   527→
   528→**Concurrent Sessions:**
   529→
   530→- When a second session starts in the same directory while another has uncommitted checkpoints, a warning is shown
   531→- Both sessions can proceed - their checkpoints interleave on the same shadow branch
   532→- Each session's `RewindPoint` includes `SessionID` and `SessionPrompt` to help identify which checkpoint belongs to which session
   533→- On commit, all sessions are condensed together with archived sessions in numbered subfolders
   534→- Note: Different git worktrees have separate shadow branches (worktree-specific naming), so concurrent sessions in different worktrees do not conflict
   535→
   536→**Orphaned Shadow Branches:**
   537→
   538→- A shadow branch is "orphaned" if it exists but has no corresponding session state file
   539→- This can happen if the state file is manually deleted or lost
   540→- When a new session starts with an orphaned branch, the branch is automatically reset
   541→- If the existing session DOES have a state file (concurrent session in same directory), a `SessionIDConflictError` is returned
   542→
   543→**Shadow Branch Migration (Pull/Rebase):**
   544→
   545→- If user does stash → pull → apply (or rebase), HEAD changes but work isn't committed
   546→- The shadow branch would be orphaned at the old commit
   547→- Detection: base commit changed AND old shadow branch still exists (would be deleted if user committed)
   548→- Action: shadow branch is renamed from `entire/<old-hash>-<worktreeHash>` to `entire/<new-hash>-<worktreeHash>`
   549→- Session continues seamlessly with checkpoints preserved
   550→
   551→#### When Modifying Strategies
   552→
   553→- All strategies must implement the full `Strategy` interface
   554→- Register new strategies in `init()` using `Register()`
   555→- Test with `mise run test` - strategy tests are in `*_test.go` files
   556→- **Update both CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md** when adding or modifying strategies to keep documentation current
   557→
   558→# Important Notes
   559→
   560→- **Before committing:** Follow the "Before Every Commit (REQUIRED)" checklist above - CI will fail without it
   561→- Integration tests: run `mise run test:integration` when changing integration test code
   562→- When adding new features, ensure they are well-tested and documented.
   563→- Always check for code duplication and refactor as needed.
   564→
   565→## Go Code Style
   566→
   567→- Write lint-compliant Go code on the first attempt. Before outputting Go code, mentally verify it passes `golangci-lint` (or your specific linter).
   568→- Follow standard Go idioms: proper error handling, no unused variables/imports, correct formatting (gofmt), meaningful names.
   569→- Handle all errors explicitly—don't leave them unchecked.
   570→- Reference `.golangci.yml` for enabled linters before writing Go code.
   571→
   572→## Accessibility
   573→
   574→The CLI supports an accessibility mode for users who rely on screen readers. This mode uses simpler text prompts instead of interactive TUI elements.
   575→
   576→### Environment Variable
   577→
   578→- `ACCESSIBLE=1` (or any non-empty value) enables accessibility mode
   579→- Users can set this in their shell profile (`.bashrc`, `.zshrc`) for persistent use
   580→
   581→### Implementation Guidelines
   582→
   583→When adding new interactive forms or prompts using `huh`:
   584→
   585→**In the `cli` package:**
   586→Use `NewAccessibleForm()` instead of `huh.NewForm()`:
   587→
   588→```go
   589→// Good - respects ACCESSIBLE env var
   590→form := NewAccessibleForm(
   591→    huh.NewGroup(
   592→        huh.NewSelect[string]().
   593→            Title("Choose an option").
   594→            Options(...).
   595→            Value(&choice),
   596→    ),
   597→)
   598→
   599→// Bad - ignores accessibility setting
   600→form := huh.NewForm(...)
   601→```
   602→
   603→**In the `strategy` package:**
   604→Use the `isAccessibleMode()` helper. Note that `WithAccessible()` is only available on forms, not individual fields, so wrap confirmations in a form:
   605→
   606→```go
   607→form := huh.NewForm(
   608→    huh.NewGroup(
   609→        huh.NewConfirm().
   610→            Title("Confirm action?").
   611→            Value(&confirmed),
   612→    ),
   613→)
   614→if isAccessibleMode() {
   615→    form = form.WithAccessible(true)
   616→}
   617→if err := form.Run(); err != nil { ... }
   618→```
   619→
   620→### Key Points
   621→
   622→- Always use the accessibility helpers for any `huh` forms/prompts
   623→- Test new interactive features with `ACCESSIBLE=1` to ensure they work
   624→- The accessible mode is documented in `--help` output
   625→

    54→

    57→```

   103→
   104→## Key Concepts
   105→
   106→### Sessions
   107→
   108→A **session** represents a complete interaction with your AI agent, from start to finish. Each session captures all prompts, responses, files modified, and timestamps.
   109→
   110→**Session ID format:** `YYYY-MM-DD-<UUID>` (e.g., `2026-01-08-abc123de-f456-7890-abcd-ef1234567890`)
   111→
   112→Sessions are stored separately from your code commits on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch.
   113→
   114→### Checkpoints
   115→
   116→A **checkpoint** is a snapshot within a session that you can rewind to—a "save point" in your work.
   117→
   118→**When checkpoints are created:**
   119→
   120→- **Manual-commit strategy**: When you or the agent make a git commit
   121→- **Auto-commit strategy**: After each agent response
   122→
   123→**Checkpoint IDs** are 12-character hex strings (e.g., `a3b2c4d5e6f7`).
   124→
   125→### How It Works
   126→
   127→```
   128→Your Branch                    entire/checkpoints/v1
   129→     │                                  │
   130→     ▼                                  │
   131→[Base Commit]                           │
   132→     │                                  │
   133→     │  ┌─── Agent works ───┐           │
   134→     │  │  Step 1           │           │
   135→     │  │  Step 2           │           │
   136→     │  │  Step 3           │           │
   137→     │  └───────────────────┘           │
   138→     │                                  │
   139→     ▼                                  ▼
   140→[Your Commit] ─────────────────► [Session Metadata]
   141→     │                           (transcript, prompts,
   142→     │                            files touched)
   143→     ▼
   144→```
   145→
   146→Checkpoints are saved as you work. When you commit, session metadata is permanently stored on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch and linked to your commit.
   147→
   148→### Strategies
   149→
   150→Entire offers two strategies for capturing your work:
   151→
   152→| Aspect              | Manual-Commit                            | Auto-Commit                                        |
   153→| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
   154→| Code commits        | None on your branch                      | Created automatically after each agent response    |
   155→| Safe on main branch | Yes                                      | Use caution - creates commits on active branch     |
   156→| Rewind              | Always possible, non-destructive         | Full rewind on feature branches; logs-only on main |
   157→| Best for            | Most workflows - keeps git history clean | Teams wanting automatic code commits               |
   158→
   159→### Git Worktrees
   160→
   161→Entire works seamlessly with [git worktrees](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree). Each worktree has independent session tracking, so you can run multiple AI sessions in different worktrees without conflicts.
   162→
   163→### Concurrent Sessions
   164→
   165→Multiple AI sessions can run on the same commit. If you start a second session while another has uncommitted work, Entire warns you and tracks them separately. Both sessions' checkpoints are preserved and can be rewound independently.
   166→
   167→## Commands Reference
   168→
   169→| Command          | Description                                                                                       |
   170→| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   171→| `entire clean`   | Clean up orphaned Entire data                                                                     |
   172→| `entire disable` | Remove Entire hooks from repository                                                               |
   173→| `entire doctor`  | Fix or clean up stuck sessions                                                                    |
   174→| `entire enable`  | Enable Entire in your repository (uses `manual-commit` by default)                                |
   175→| `entire explain` | Explain a session or commit                                                                       |
   176→| `entire reset`   | Delete the shadow branch and session state for the current HEAD commit                            |
   177→| `entire resume`  | Switch to a branch, restore latest checkpointed session metadata, and show command(s) to continue |
   178→| `entire rewind`  | Rewind to a previous checkpoint                                                                   |
   179→| `entire status`  | Show current session and strategy info                                                            |
   180→| `entire version` | Show Entire CLI version                                                                           |
   181→
   182→### `entire enable` Flags
   183→
   184→| Flag                   | Description                                                           |
   185→| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   186→| `--agent <name>`       | AI agent to install hooks for: `claude-code`, `gemini`, or `opencode` |
   187→| `--force`, `-f`        | Force reinstall hooks (removes existing Entire hooks first)           |

   198→

   201→```

   203→## Configuration
   204→
   205→Entire uses two configuration files in the `.entire/` directory:
   206→
   207→### settings.json (Project Settings)
   208→
   209→Shared across the team, typically committed to git:
   210→
   211→```json
   212→{
   213→  "strategy": "manual-commit",
   214→  "enabled": true
   215→}
   216→```
   217→

   219→

   221→
   222→```json
   223→{
   224→  "enabled": false,
   225→  "log_level": "debug"
   226→}
   227→```
   228→
   229→### Configuration Options
   230→
   231→| Option                               | Values                           | Description                                          |

   233→| `enabled`                            | `true`, `false`                  | Enable/disable Entire                                |
   234→| `log_level`                          | `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error` | Logging verbosity                                    |

   236→| `strategy_options.push_sessions`     | `true`, `false`                  | Auto-push `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch on git push |

   242→Each agent stores its hook configuration in its own directory. When you run `entire enable`, hooks are installed in the appropriate location for each selected agent:

   244→| Agent       | Hook Location                 | Format            |
   245→| ----------- | ----------------------------- | ----------------- |

   247→| Gemini CLI  | `.gemini/settings.json`       | JSON hooks config |

   251→
   252→### Auto-Summarization
   253→
   254→When enabled, Entire automatically generates AI summaries for checkpoints at commit time. Summaries capture intent, outcome, learnings, friction points, and open items from the session.

   259→    "summarize": {

   261→    }
   262→  }
   263→}

   270→
   271→**Note:** Currently uses Claude CLI for summary generation. Other AI backends may be supported in future versions.
   272→
   273→### Settings Priority
   274→
   275→Local settings override project settings field-by-field. When you run `entire status`, it shows both project and local (effective) settings.
   276→
   277→### Gemini CLI
   278→
   279→Gemini CLI support is currently in preview. Entire can work with [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) as an alternative to Claude Code, or alongside it — you can have multiple agents' hooks enabled at the same time.

   281→To enable:

   283→```bash

   287→All commands (`rewind`, `status`, `doctor`, etc.) work the same regardless of which agent is configured.
   288→
   289→If you run into any issues with Gemini CLI integration, please [open an issue](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues).
   290→
   291→### OpenCode
   292→
   293→OpenCode support is currently in preview. Entire can work with [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/docs/cli/) as an alternative to Claude Code, or alongside it — you can have multiple agents' hooks enabled at the same time.
   294→
   295→To enable:
   296→
   297→```bash
   298→entire enable --agent opencode
   299→```
   300→
   301→Or select OpenCode from the interactive agent picker when running `entire enable`.
   302→
   303→All commands (`rewind`, `status`, `doctor`, etc.) work the same regardless of which agent is configured.
   304→
   305→If you run into any issues with OpenCode integration, please [open an issue](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues).
   306→
   307→## Security & Privacy
   308→
   309→**Your session transcripts are stored in your git repository** on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. If your repository is public, this data is visible to anyone.
   310→
   311→Entire automatically redacts detected secrets (API keys, tokens, credentials) when writing to `entire/checkpoints/v1`, but redaction is best-effort. Temporary shadow branches used during a session may contain unredacted data and should not be pushed. See [docs/security-and-privacy.md](docs/security-and-privacy.md) for details.

   313→## Troubleshooting

   315→### Common Issues

   317→| Issue                    | Solution                                                |
   318→| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- |
   319→| "Not a git repository"   | Navigate to a Git repository first                      |
   320→| "Entire is disabled"     | Run `entire enable`                                     |
   321→| "No rewind points found" | Work with your configured agent and commit your changes |
   322→| "shadow branch conflict" | Run `entire reset --force`                              |

   334→```

   337→```

   339→### Debug Mode

   341→```

   344→

   346→{
   347→  "log_level": "debug"
   348→}
   349→```

   371→
   372→## Development

   374→This project uses [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/) for task automation and dependency management.
